target_customer: Genetic testing companies, national governments and pharma companies comparing large populations of genomes
problem: Comparing whole genomes at population scale needs specialized assembly and data mining software to power diagnostics and drug target discovery.
business_model: Genomic analysis software licensed to testing labs, governments and pharma

founders.name: Adina Mangubat
education: University of Washington (psychology degree, per GeekWire profile summary)
founders.background_notes: Forbes 30 Under 30 for Science and Healthcare (2013) per YC page. A 2013 Crosscut piece described her as on her third startup. Distributed computing background per GeekWire profile summary.

technical_complexity.rationale: Large scale genome assembly and variant analysis with machine learning is computationally and algorithmically hard, though the team had years of work (Anchored Assembly, BioGraph) before 2019.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary assembly algorithms and genomic expertise, but cloud genomics platforms and open tools compete.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Omicia acquired Spiral Genetics in 2017, then per a search summary the founder bought it back in early 2019 and relaunched with a Microsoft Azure partnership for heart disease prediction (GeekWire 2019).

market_need_then: Genomic data volume was growing and testing companies, governments and pharma were building population genomics programs; the 2019 GeekWire relaunch story links the work to predicting heart disease from genomes.

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by GeekWire, Xconomy and Crosscut in 2011 to 2013 and 2017 to 2019; CEO named to Forbes 30 Under 30.

brand_strength.rationale: Solid regional press and an evocative double helix name, but no evidence of community or brand driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Spiral Genetics raised a $3M Series A led by DFJ in 2013 and was acquired by Omicia in January 2017 for an undisclosed price. A search summary says the founder bought it back in early 2019 and it joined YC in Winter 2019 and relaunched with a Microsoft partnership. YC now lists it Inactive, but no shutdown or later outcome source was found, so the cause is not public.
notes: No company website on YC; treated as dead or unlisted. The GeekWire 2019 page returned 403, so buyback and relaunch details come from search result summaries. Crosscut states total raised $3.7M, which exceeds the $3M Series A, so about $0.7M of earlier money (a convertible note per one database) is unrecorded. Databases give $3.2M to $4.4M totals; not recorded as rounds. Series A and the $3M amount are confirmed by BioSpace and Xconomy. Exit type is acquisition (2017) but YC status is Inactive and the 2019 buyback is not reflected. Competitors left empty because the search for dated 2018 to 2019 competitors returned only current comparison pages.
